result:
Status: I've gathered the evidence from the repo and the run logs. I'm reporting now, because the one check I haven't run (a live reproduction) would write files.

## Root cause

**The failure is not a bug in a mod. It is how the engine's `$.model.fork` behaves, and the mods already work around it.** I could not confirm the mechanism from the generated declarations, so the engine-side explanation below is inferred.

- **What `fork` does.** The `runs/2026-10-02-handoff-model-pin/PLAN.md:13` entry describes `$.model.fork({ prompt })` as one tool-less question "over this session's own transcript (same model and system prompt, served from the prompt cache)". Its documented failure reasons include `nothing-to-fork`.
- **Where it fails.** In a resumed session (`claude -p --continue`, or `/resume`), the transcript exists on disk but the engine has no live request to fork from. `AGENTS.md:135` says this happens on the first command, so the engine most likely builds the fork base from the session's last request. The `bws-cockpit/hooks/register.tsx:677` comment says it directly: "A resumed session has a transcript but nothing to fork until its first request."
- **The `session.start` theory doesn't hold.** `session.start` doesn't run after `/resume`, but the fork needs no mod-side setup. The missing piece is engine state, not anything a mod initialises.
- **First observed.** `runs/2026-10-02-handoff-model-pin/RUNLOG.md:33` records "Run 1 failed: with `claude -p --continue "/handoff"`, the resumed session had nothing to fork, so no handoff was written."

## Error text

The result is `{ isAnswered: false, reason: 'nothing-to-fork' }`. It is returned as a value, not thrown.

## Where it's handled

- `bws-cockpit/hooks/register.tsx:676-683`: forks, then falls back to `$.session.messages()` plus `$.model.complete` on the session model.
- `bws-kit/classify-fork.ts:108-129` (`runFork`): the same fallback, vendored into bws-memory, bws-diagram, bws-direction and bws-enhance.
- `bws-memory/hooks/register.tsx:121,201` and `bws-diagram/hooks/register.tsx:67` call `$.model.fork` directly.
- `bws-kit/classify-fork.ts:118`: when the transcript is empty, the fallback returns `nothing-to-fork` with "no messages to work from".

## Checks I could and couldn't do

- **Version.** `claude --version` reports **2.1.309**. The AGENTS.md baseline is 2.1.296, and its recent-work range is 2.1.302–2.1.303. I did not check whether 2.1.309 changed fork behaviour.
- **Generated declarations.** There is no `.claude-plugin/types/` in this worktree (it is gitignored and generated), and `docs/mods.md` doesn't mention `fork`. I could not read the real signature or any documented session requirement. The signature I have is from the repo's own wrapper, `fork: (request: { prompt: string }) => Promise<ModelReply | { isAnswered: false; reason: 'nothing-to-fork' }>` (`bws-kit/classify-fork.ts:22`).
- **Reproduction.** I did not reproduce it live. The existing tests (`bws-cockpit/tests/handoff.test.ts:138,162`, `bws-kit/tests/classify-fork.test.ts:125-149`) stub `model.fork` to return `nothing-to-fork`. They test the fallback, not the engine's behaviour. `claude plugin test` would also regenerate the types folder, which breaks your no-file-changes rule. A real repro means `claude -p --continue "/handoff"` in a project with a prior session. The `RUNLOG.md:33` entry is the only recorded live failure.

Next step if you want one: I can run the live headless repro in a scratch folder, or generate the types somewhere outside the repo to confirm the signature.
